recentItems.title: Chile 0-0 England (1984)
recentItems.description: Looking back 30 years this month to England's 0-0 draw away to Chile in June 1984. The match marks the last match of England's South American tour at the end of the 1983/84 season, having famously beaten Brazil 2-0 a week earlier before losing 2-0 to Uruguay. The match against Chile sees England create the majority of chances, with captain Bryan Robson giving a typically ferocious performance, but they are unable to break the deadlock.

recentItems.title: Poland 1-1 England (1991) ECQ
recentItems.description: England qualify for Euro 92 - just! - after a late Gary Lineker goal earns them a draw away to Poland in November 1991. In a very tight qualifying group, England go into the match needing a draw to qualify but know defeat will put them out with both the Republic of Ireland and Poland breathing down their necks. Good fortune is on their side as the Poles have a strong penalty shout turned down minutes before Lineker's equaliser.

recentItems.title: 1983 FA Cup Final pre-match coverage (BBC)
recentItems.description: Ahead of the FA Cup Final tomorrow, a look back to 1983 and nearly 10 minutes of build-up from shortly before Brighton & Hove Albion's clash with Manchester United. Includes a run through of the two teams and the thoughts of BBC pundits Bobby Charlton, Jimmy Hill and Lawrie McMenamy with David Coleman - despite the confidence of the panel United would win it, Brighton would famously almost win this match ("and Smith must score...") before being thrashed in the replay. I don't have any more coverage of this sorry.

recentItems.title: Netherlands 2-0 England (1993) WCQ
recentItems.description:
England's World Cup qualification hopes are dealt a shattering blow as they lose 2-0 away to Holland in October 1993. In what is effectively a winner takes all clash, Graham Taylor is left furious with the referee over his failure to send off Ronald Koeman for hauling down a goalbound David Platt - Koeman going on to put the Dutch ahead before Dennis Bergkamp settles it. Earlier Holland's Frank Rijkaard had controversially had a goal ruled out for offside. England's only hope of qualifying would now be if the Dutch lost away to Poland and they thrashed San Marino in the final game.

(Properly watching this match for the first time in over 20 years, I'd forgotten just how open this game actually was given so much was at stake. England carved out several decent opportunities and the Dutch, with flying wingers Overmars and Roy, always looked dangerous going forward - that save in the second half by David Seaman to deny Rijkaard from point blank range was tremendous but ultimately long since forgotten due to the result).

recentItems.title: England 1-3 Brazil (1995)
recentItems.description: Despite taking the lead through a tremendous Graeme Le Saux goal, England are beaten 3-1 at Wembley by Brazil in June 1995 as emerging talents such as Ronaldo and Juninho shine. The result means the World Cup holders lift the Umbro Cup, which Sweden and Japan also contested, and condemns Terry Venables to his only defeat from open play in charge of England (although they had been losing away to Republic of Ireland when their match was abandoned).

recentItems.title: England 1-0 Nigeria (1994)
recentItems.description: England's first meeting with Nigeria is an entertaining friendly at Wembley in November 1994. The visitors impress with their skill but the match is decided in England's favour by a goal from David Platt, on a night when midfield colleague Dennis Wise gives arguably his best international performance and central defenders Neil Ruddock and Steve Howey make their debuts. Includes some post-match thoughts of pundits Alan Hansen and Jimmy Hill with Des Lynam. The result means England complete 1994 unbeaten (albeit after just six matches, all at home!).

recentItems.title: England 1-1 Romania (1994)
recentItems.description: England concede a goal for the first time under Terry Venables but preserve their unbeaten record under him by drawing 1-1 with an impressive Romania side at Wembley in October 1994. Robert Lee marks his full England debut by equalising on the stroke of half time after Ilie Dumitrescu had put the Romanians ahead.

recentItems.title: FA Cup semi-final goals 1984-88
recentItems.description:
Ahead of FA Cup semi-final weekend, a look back at all the semi-finals played between 1984 and 1988. Includes memories such as Everton narrowly winning three successive semi-finals from 1984 to 1986, Manchester United, Coventry City and Wimbledon coming from behind en route to winning the cup, Liverpool moving towards the double in 1986 and 3rd Division Plymouth pushing Watford hard in the 1984 semi-final but losing out.

(I've had slight probs with the audio on a couple of matches so you might need to adjust your speakers slightly along the way, thanks).

recentItems.title: England and Republic of Ireland prepare for Euro 88
recentItems.description: On the eve of the start of Euro 88, a look ahead to England and Republic of Ireland's chances from ITV's preview show - includes live interviews from managers Bobby Robson and Jack Charlton and the views of studio guests Brian Clough and Trevor Francis with Nick Owen. England were fancying their chances of success in West Germany but they would infamously lose all three group games, including to Ireland in their opening match as the Irish only narrowly missed out on a semi-final spot.

recentItems.title: England 2-2 Argentina (1991)
recentItems.description: In their first meeting since their infamous World Cup quarter-final five years earlier, England and Argentina draw 2-2 at Wembley in May 1991. The result wins England the England Challenge Cup (also contested for with USSR) but there is disappointment after throwing away a 2-0 lead to set-piece goals. Earlier Gary Lineker and David Platt score for England. Includes the post-match comments of Gary Lineker, Graham Taylor and Jimmy Hill.

recentItems.title: England, Scotland and Northern Ireland prepare for 1986 World Cup
recentItems.description: Shown on the eve of the 1986 World Cup, a preview of England, Scotland and Northern Ireland's chances in Mexico. Includes interviews with English and Northern Irish management and squad members and the views of ITV panelists including Kevin Keegan, Mick Channon, Bryan Hamilton, Billy McNeill, Ron Atkinson and David Pleat with the late Brian Moore, poking fun at Channon's inability to pronounce Lineker!

recentItems.title: England 0-0 Colombia (1995)
recentItems.description: No goals but plenty of entertainment as Colombia visit Wembley for a friendly in September 1995. The match is forever remembered for visiting goalkeeper Rene Higuita's 'scorpion kick' save, as the Colombians (like on their previous visit in 1988) entertain the small crowd with their style of football. England put on a good attacking display despite not scoring, hitting the woodwork three times. Includes post-match interviews and some thoughts of studio pundit Jimmy Hill.
